message:
Summary: {
"USER_CONTEXT": "Generate a proof-of-concept (PoC) for a vulnerability in the Unicorn engine where cpuid results are hardcoded rather than set by the selected CPU. The PoC must be a single raw input file (binary or text) that triggers the vulnerability. Submit both the PoC and a candidate trace using: bash ./submit.sh PATH_TO_POC /workspace/candidate_trace.json",
"COMPLETED": "Explored repository structure and identified the vulnerable code in /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/unicorn/qemu/target/i386/cpu.c (cpu_x86_cpuid function) and misc_helper.c (helper_cpuid). Confirmed cpuid values are hardcoded based on CPU model definitions rather than actual host CPU.",
"PENDING": "Create the PoC input file that triggers the vulnerability. Write the candidate trace file. Submit both files using the provided submit script.",
"CURRENT_STATE": "Working directory: /workspace. Vulnerable source: /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/unicorn/. The cpuid function uses hardcoded values from CPU model definitions (e.g., env->cpuid_level, env->cpuid_version, env->cpuid_vendor1/2/3) instead of querying the actual CPU. The vulnerability can be triggered by executing a cpuid instruction in emulated x86 code.",
"CODE_STATE": "Key files: /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/unicorn/qemu/target/i386/cpu.c (cpu_x86_cpuid function, lines 3990-4400), /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/unicorn/qemu/target/i386/misc_helper.c (helper_cpuid function, lines 105-140). The cpuid results are populated from env->cpuid_* fields which are set from CPU model definitions (x86_cpu_load_model).",
"TESTS": "No tests run yet. Need to create a PoC that demonstrates the hardcoded cpuid behavior.",
"CHANGES": "No code changes made yet.",
"DEPS": "Unicorn engine (C library). The PoC will likely be a binary file containing x86 machine code that executes the cpuid instruction.",
"VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS": "Repository: /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/unicorn. No git operations performed yet."
}
